statements.quote: Participants were instructed to generate eight unique ideas for each task within 30 min. The ideas were to be expressed through sketching and a brief description on an A5 paper for each. Each sheet used a template that designated the specific areas for drawing the idea and writing the description. Additionally, the template anonymously identified each idea by a numerical code corresponding to the task number, the student's numerical ID and the idea number. For example, the fifth idea from task 2, developed by a student with ID 16, would be coded as 02_016_5.
statements.locator: p. 6, section 4.3.1, Session 1: Controlled Experiment (idea template and identifiers)

statements.quote: Figures 2 and 3 present four examples of ideas produced during the experiment by two students, demonstrating how they applied the provided template for each task, both with and without the help of ChatGPT.
statements.locator: pp. 7-8, section 4.3.1, paragraph introducing Figures 2 and 3

statements.quote: The questionnaire was created using Google Forms, following the structure detailed in Table 2.

The second session was dedicated to the evaluation of the outcomes from T1 and T2. The evaluation instrument was transferred to Google Forms, providing students with a user‐friendly and digital assessment format. Each form page included a text field where students had to specify the ID of the idea they were evaluating, a crucial step for the subsequent categorization and analysis. Additionally, each page included a multiple‐choice grid displaying the items related to the measured variables, along with the associated Likert scale for scoring them.

notes:
Checked 2026-10-09. Read the entire 706-line markdown conversion of the 19-page publisher version of record, including the end matter and references; the document contains no appendix. Verified the availability statement against PDF page 17 and the quoted material descriptions against PDF pages 5-9. No preregistration, supplementary-file reference, data-repository link, or code-release link was found. The form's data_url and code_url are empty. PDF link annotations contain no study-data repository URL, and the PDF has no embedded attachments.

The explicit page-17 statement supports status on_request. No public deposit attributable to c201 was confirmed; deposits is therefore empty. Author requests are not repository deposits, and no author was contacted. In-paper instruments, four example ideas from two students (Figures 2-3), and selected qualitative quotations (Table 5) are not the full participant/output dataset. The Software and Resources credits identify contributions, not released files.

No public data were available for computing the missing participant-level means, SDs, SEs, analyzed counts by condition/task/randomized sequence, paired or clustered uncertainty, or text/idea diversity. The paper describes idea identifiers encoding task, student and idea number (p. 6) and ratings linked to idea IDs (p. 8), but these linked records and the full idea corpus were not obtained. Consequently none of final.open_items was resolved by public data; what_we_could_compute is null.

Publisher check: https://doi.org/10.1002/cae.22817 returned HTTP 302 to https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cae.22817, which returned HTTP 403 and a Cloudflare bot check. No attempt was made to pass it. Search counts are returned API totals, not counts of relevant deposits. Failed Zenodo size=100 requests are recorded as null and were followed by successful anonymous size=25 requests. No GitHub repository was named or queried.

Broad OSF search verification: https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/rzk9x/contributors/, https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/rzk9x/files/osfstorage/, and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/rzk9x/children/ each returned HTTP 200 (one anonymous contributor, four files, zero child nodes). File list: Study 3_data.sav (14240 bytes); Study 1_data.sav (13330 bytes); Pretest_data.sav (11200 bytes); Study 2_data.sav (14560 bytes). https://osf.io/rzk9x/ returned HTTP 200. The public file https://osf.io/download/3b2yr/ returned HTTP 200 and was read only in memory with pyreadstat; 190 rows were observed with columns Type, Group, Ho1, Ho2, Con1, Con2, Con3, An1, An2, An3, Mea1, Mea2, Mea3, Mea4, Frequency, Attitude, Gender, Age, Edu, Income, Ho_AV, Con2_AV, An3_AV, Mea_AV. Its title, multi-study file structure, and observed variables do not identify c201; no connection was confirmed, so it is excluded from this paper's deposits.

Also checked https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/bqdsn/contributors/, https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/bqdsn/files/osfstorage/, and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/bqdsn/children/: each returned HTTP 200 (one contributor, Nidhi Nasiar; zero files; zero children). Its graduate-education virtual-teaching-assistant study differs from c201.

Confidence is medium for the overall public-availability assessment because the publisher supplement area was blocked and the specified OSF endpoint searches project titles rather than contributor names. The paper's on-request statement is explicit. All network requests used Python urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1; no login, access request, CAPTCHA interaction, or account creation was attempted. No downloaded data were saved.
